speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: I will now bring Members through the specifics of the Agreement on the Realignment of the Boundary between the Jakarta Flight Information Region (FIR) and the Singapore FIR and respond to the various questions from Members on the considerations, implications and the way forward for the FIR Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Every state has its own territorial airspace over which it has sovereignty.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Then, there are Flight Information Regions (FIRs), which are blocks of airspace assigned by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) to air navigation services (ANS) providers, such as the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS), for the purpose of managing civil air traffic.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: FIRs do not have to follow territorial boundaries.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The provision of ANS around the world falls into three broad models.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The first is where the state provides ANS for an FIR that is within its territorial airspace.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: For example, the Aeronautical Radio of Thailand Limited (Aerothai) provides ANS for Thai airspace within the Bangkok FIR.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The second is where the state provides ANS within its FIR, but the FIR extends beyond its territorial airspace.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: For example, Indonesia provides ANS over Christmas Island, which is part of Australia's airspace but within the Jakarta FIR.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Likewise, the US provides ANS over Canadian airspace within US FIRs.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The third is where the state provides ANS in the FIR and territorial airspace of a neighbouring state.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: For example, in order to manage traffic for Geneva Airport, Switzerland provides air traffic services for French airspace that is part of the Marseille FIR through a delegation arrangement.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: So, territorial airspace, FIRs and the provision of ANS.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: These come together across the world in different models.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But regardless of the model adopted, the paramount objective is to ensure the safety and efficiency of international civil aviation in accordance with ICAO rules.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The FIR issue has been on the Indonesia-Singapore bilateral agenda for several decades.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Its resolution will bring clarity not just to both countries, but also to the international civil aviation community.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It would also lay the foundation for us to strengthen bilateral cooperation in the aviation sector and across our broader relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Singapore and Indonesia, therefore, agreed to discuss the FIR issue as an integral part of a broader framework, endorsed by Prime Minister Lee and President Jokowi, to achieve a durable and balanced set of agreements that meets both sides' core interests.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Our aim was to: first, uphold the safety and efficiency of international civil aviation; second, meet Indonesia's desire to align the FIR boundaries to correspond with its territorial airspace; and third, accommodate current traffic and future growth of Changi and Indonesian airports.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The negotiations entailed significant involvement and commitment at all levels of Government, given the strategic, political, operational and technical considerations.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Based on the parameters endorsed by the two Leaders, Coordinating Ministers, Ministers and officials from multiple agencies were involved in the negotiations.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: MOT/CAAS officials, especially ANS experts, worked closely with their Indonesian counterparts to address the complex technical details, taking into account ICAO rules.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The outcome of this consultative negotiation process is an FIR Agreement that ensures the safety and efficiency of air traffic, addresses Indonesia and Singapore's interests and needs, and benefits international civil aviation.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Mr Gerald Giam asked about the air traffic arrangements under the FIR Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Third, under the delegation arrangement, CAAS will provide ANS, such as air traffic services, publication of aeronautical information and designing of air routes within the airspace where the provision of ANS has been delegated to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The FIR Agreement also caters for civil-military cooperation in air traffic management, based on ICAO provisions.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Indonesia and Singapore will consult each other and ICAO prior to the end of the 25 years, to ensure safety and efficiency of international civil aviation beyond the 25 years.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Ms Poh Li San, Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Melvin Yong, Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Mr Gerald Giam asked about the implications of the FIR Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan also asked the same in a question for written response.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It clarifies how ANS will be provided in this busy and complex airspace and ensures that air traffic flows in our region, including to and from Changi and Indonesian airports, will continue to be safe and efficient.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Every major airport in the world has a contiguous block of airspace for its arrival and departure procedures, which is essential for ensuring safety.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It is necessary to deconflict aircraft when they are taking off or landing, which are critical phases of flight and when safety risks are the highest.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Changi Airport, for example, had nearly 400,000 flights each year pre-COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It will support the continued growth and competitiveness of Singapore's air hub and aviation-related sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The FIR Agreement will also ensure the safe and efficient management of traffic to Indonesian airports, including Batam, Bintan and Tanjung Pinang airports, which are in close proximity to Changi.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The international civil aviation community will also benefit.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The International Air Transport Association forecasts that air traffic in the Asia-Pacific will have the highest growth globally over the next 20 years.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: With the FIR Agreement and closer bilateral cooperation, airlines and other aviation stakeholders will have more opportunities to tap on the future growth in air traffic in this region, grow their operations, connect more passengers, attract more investments and create more jobs in our regional aviation sector.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Ms Poh Li San and Mr Melvin Yong asked about the implementation of the FIR Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As explained by Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean, the FIR Agreement, Defence Cooperation Agreement and Extradition Treaty are to be brought into force and implemented simultaneously.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: For the FIR Agreement, first, the domestic processes for both sides to ratify all three agreements have to be completed.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Fourth, once the FIR boundary realignment and delegation arrangements are approved by ICAO, Indonesia and Singapore will agree on a date to implement the FIR Agreement and for all the three agreements to enter into force together.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Mr Pritam Singh and Mr Saktiandi Supaat also asked what will happen after the 25-year duration of the FIR Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean has spoken on this.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We will have 25 years to implement the FIR Agreement and gain experience from the new arrangements.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It will allow both sides to strengthen our bilateral transport ties and it establishes a foundation for further cooperation in the provision of ANS and in other areas.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The aviation sector will continue to develop with advancements in technology and ANS procedures.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As air traffic and airports grow, our operational needs and aviation standards will also evolve.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: All these elements will shape the circumstances under which we will make decisions in the future.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Singapore and Indonesia have agreed to consult each other and ICAO before the end of the 25 years, to ensure the safety and efficiency of international civil aviation beyond the 25-year duration.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We were able to achieve this outcome because both sides approached the negotiations with a shared commitment to uphold the safety and efficiency and support the growth of international civil aviation.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It has also laid a firm foundation for closer cooperation in aviation and other areas between Indonesia and Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In closing, I would like to express our deep appreciation to the negotiating teams from Singapore and Indonesia, in particular, our MOT and CAAS officers, for their hard work in concluding the agreement and achieving an outcome that is good for Singapore, Indonesia and international civil aviation.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I have one supplementary question as a follow-up to my Parliamentary Question, which is listed as Question No 5 in the Order Paper.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: What vis-à-vis the Framework Agreement is the dispute resolution clause in the event either Singapore or Indonesia cannot come to an agreement after the end of the 25-year period?

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: This is an indication of how both countries can work together and work their own domestic processes for the joint benefit of both countries.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: For the FIR, Singapore will certainly continue to discharge its responsibilities to provide air navigation services in a safe and efficient way for civil air traffic.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: On the point of what the Senior Minister has said, the focus is to get the expanded agreement in force.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, I guess the question is what is being done now to ensure that those agreements will come into force?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: How do we get these three agreements into force?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: On another question: the Minister for Transport had indicated that these agreements, like the FIR, will benefit Changi Airport and Singapore.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: But could the Minister provide more information and details on how these would benefit both Changi Airport as well as Singapore?

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: On bringing the three agreements into force simultaneously, as I have said in my Statement, both Prime Minister Lee and President Jokowi have expressed the desire to bring these three agreements into force as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Each side will have to go through their own domestic ratification processes, and I do understand that Indonesia has already commenced this process.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: We are also going through the process on our side.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, if I may underscore a point that I made earlier, this is an agreement that does not just benefit Changi Airport, it actually also benefits Indonesian airports, for example, Batam, Bintan and Tanjung Pinang and, perhaps most crucially, it also benefits international civil aviation on the point of ensuring its safety and efficiency.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And once we keep that as the baseline, then we can look ahead because what it means is that despite all the forecasts for growth in aviation in the Asia Pacific region, unless we are able to ensure traffic is managed well, smoothly and, most importantly, safely, we will not be able to benefit collectively or individually from that growth.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, what this agreement does is that it not only gives us clarity on an important matter for both sides but also for the international aviation community which has a strong interest in this matter.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: With that as the foundation, we can then proceed to work on other important initiatives, whether it is investment in technology, infrastructure and also building closer cooperation between Indonesia and Singapore, in terms of aviation cooperation and, of course, extending beyond that into other areas.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I would say that, at its core, this agreement, once it has gone through the entire process and comes into force, it will provide clarity, certainty and, therefore, give confidence to all parties involved to then proceed with the necessary initiatives to prepare for the growth in aviation in our part of the world.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I think these agreements are very good for both Singapore and Indonesia.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The intention is for all the agreements to come into force at the same time.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: But if, in the ratification process, say, only one or two get ratified and one or two did not, what will happen to all three agreements in that situation?

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: It is because the negotiations were conducted concurrently and it has achieved a good balance of benefits across all three agreements.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Hence, both countries have agreed that the best way to resolve these three outstanding issues is to discuss them together, come to agreements on them at the same time and then to bring them into force concurrently.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: That will provide a resolution to all these three outstanding issues at the same time.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: I think that will bring many benefits to both countries so that it will reduce any chances of misunderstandings and provide a very strong basis for future cooperation.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: I should say that in any negotiation, of course, each side would want to push for its maximum benefits.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: But to have a good outcome, each side also has to look at the wider benefits, the wider interests that come from working together and arriving at an agreement, rather than not having an agreement.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: So, I think that in these negotiations, both sides took that view – that it is actually in our shared interest, in our enlightened self-interests, to come to an agreement on these three outstanding issues so that we can progress our bilateral relations on a broader front.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If so, how would the change in ANS provider affect aviation safety and security, the efficiency and the status of us as an aviation hub?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Therefore, this is an agreement and, at its heart, its durability is underpinned by this set of provisions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Any deviations from this will have to be resolved through bilateral discussions and consultation and, ultimately, approval from ICAO, which will also involve consultation with stakeholders.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I think it would be premature to consider any other alternatives.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: At this point, our focus is to bring these agreements into force, operationalise them.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Because many of the questions that are being posed are hypothetical.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Because we need to implement them, understand them fully and appreciate the value and the impact they have on the way we manage collectively air navigation services.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the maps itself, I think this is something that will have to be through bilateral consultation, the decision.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: At this point, we are not releasing the maps.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I have a question for the Minister for Transport.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Specific to the arrangement of the delegation of the FIR, may I know what are the benefits direct to Singapore?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: If I may paraphrase the Member's question so that I get it clearly, it is really, specifically, how this benefits Changi Airport and Singapore, is that right?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, as I have said, there is a broader value that this agreement brings for the international civil aviation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I would say that this is not a unique consideration for Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: All airports around the world, especially major aviation hubs, will take this into account, and, in fact, it is central.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It would also be the case for Indonesia and its airports.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, whilst we are talking and focusing on Changi Airport, in particular, and our needs, I want to emphasise that this actually brings benefits for all parties, including Indonesian airports.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, specifically for us, what it means is, with that assurance, we can now focus on also a range of other initiatives which will help to enhance the services that we can provide in terms of air navigation but also others to support the broader aviation sector in Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It also means that in our discussions with aviation sector stakeholders, including potential investors and companies which want to set up operations here, we are now able to give them greater clarity on the matter and we can move forward on that basis.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We are, as the Member by virtue of her background would be aware, looking also at various investments in technology and so on, which will enable us to enhance the quality of services that we can provide from Changi Airport.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The first is in relation to what the Minister answered just now broadly.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In terms of the FIR Agreement, how does it essentially improve bilateral transport cooperation between Singapore and Indonesia, particularly bilateral aviation ties, which Minister has mentioned, but going forward beyond airports?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My second clarification is with regard to this agreement.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It definitely provides a good opportunity for both Singapore and Indonesia to work together better within the 25 years and I think also beyond the 25 years.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My clarification is on how we can actually see this as a positive outlook as we look forward in the post-25 year phase as technology changes and, particularly, in the area of air traffic control safety for both countries, Singapore and Indonesia.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think in that spirit, it is important that we see this as an opportunity to build strong, durable and mutually beneficial ties between Indonesia and Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Of course, specifically, in the context of aviation, because we are talking about the FIR Agreement here, but really as a foundation for doing more together.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, what it means is understanding – and, in fact, I made this point in my Ministerial Statement.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think that is key because it means we understand that this is the paramount objective.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Then we have our respective interests that we need to then reconcile.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Looking ahead, I think what it means is it allows both sides to now focus on operationalising the arrangement, getting more familiar with each other in terms of how we can cooperate further, building confidence and building trust.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: That is essential because, as Senior Minister Teo made it very clear, we are neighbours, and we will be neighbours well beyond 25 years.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, it is important that at the foundation of our relationship, we have that confidence and trust.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And that is the basis on which we want to go forward.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we will be working on these various initiatives and, I might add that it is very hard to anticipate the trajectory of civil aviation over two and a half decades.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: A lot has happened in the last 25 years.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Indeed, a lot has happened in the last five, six years and we must expect a lot more may happen in the next 25 years.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: If I may just give you one example.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have the Singapore Airshow on and I met with some aviation officials this morning and one of the focal points is what in the industry they call "network operational efficiencies".

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is really about how, between the aircraft avionics and the air navigation service provisions, we can optimise so as to minimise the impediments to smooth flows, because when you have those impediments caused by congestion, weather events and so on, it means aircraft have to circle, burn extra fuel and so on, and it takes on an even more significant hue when we consider these sorts of matters in the context of the broader climate change challenge and the kind of sustainability initiatives that we want to work on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I am just citing that as one example of how we can work together and there are many other areas.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But this agreement creates the foundation upon which we can build that stronger, bilateral partnership.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I just wanted to say that I think it is a great outcome for both countries and, given that it has taken us so much time to get to where we are, as the duration of the three agreements are about 25 years, I wonder whether it is possible that we could have a situation where it is an auto renewal, rather than a review followed by a renewal.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I am just changing it slightly with a view that we want to secure the future for both countries and for the global community, particularly for global travel.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And then, I think we have the time and opportunity to work on a whole slew of initiatives to foster that closer cooperation and understanding.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I think we need to focus on this first.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I would not preclude alternative structures going forward.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But neither do I want to hasten into those sorts of discussions at this point.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think, in general, from a Government point of view, what we have today is a good agreement.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Agreements can always be better, but the converse can also be true.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, it is about making sure what we have works and works well for all parties.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think that would then give us the basis on which to build for the future.
